findings.title: Tainted Sql String
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly concatenates user input into the SQL query string. By using a parameterized query, the database driver can properly escape and quote the input, preventing malicious SQL code from being executed. This fix ensures that the user input is treated as data, not as part of the SQL command.
findings.cwe: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection attacks by separating the SQL command from the user input data
findings.fixed_code: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?"; result = conn.execute(query, (user_id,)).fetchall()

findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation allows an attacker to traverse the file system by providing a filename with ../ or ..\. To fix this, we need to validate and sanitize the filename by removing any ../ or ..\ sequences. This can be achieved by using the replace method on the filename string.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group currently allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical vulnerability. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource with a specific CIDR block, we can mitigate this vulnerability and prevent unauthorized access.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: RDS instance publicly accessible
findings.description: The RDS instance is currently publicly accessible, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, the 'publicly_accessible' attribute should be set to 'false' to restrict access to the instance. This change will prevent unauthorized access to the database instance.
findings.fix_hint: Set the 'publicly_accessible' attribute to 'false' for the 'aws_db_instance' resource

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public ACL
findings.description: The current configuration allows public access to the S3 bucket, which is a critical security risk. By setting the ACL to private, only authorized users can access the bucket. This change should be applied to the aws_s3_bucket resource in the main.tf file.
findings.fix_hint: Set the ACL of the S3 bucket to private to prevent public access

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: iam:*
findings.description: The 'iam:*' action grants full control over IAM, allowing privilege escalation. Removing this action prevents unauthorized access to IAM resources. The corrected policy only includes the original 'LimitedEC2Access' statement, ensuring limited access to EC2 and other specified resources.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the 'iam:*' action from the policy to prevent full IAM control

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: Database instance has no logging. Missing logs can cause missing important event information.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Automated fix unavailable — review manually.

findings.title: Rds Insecure Password Storage In Source Code
findings.description: The hardcoded password in the aws_db_instance resource is a security risk, to mitigate this use the random_password resource to generate a random password. The random_password resource generates a random password and stores it in the result attribute, which can then be used in the aws_db_instance resource. This ensures that the password is not hardcoded in the source code.
findings.fix_hint: Use the aws_db_instance resource with a random password generated by the random_password resource

findings.title: Sql Injection Db Cursor Execute
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly concatenates user-controlled data into the query string, allowing an attacker to inject malicious SQL code. By using parameterized queries, the execute method will treat the user-controlled data as a literal value instead of part of the SQL code, preventing SQL injection. This fix ensures that the query is executed safely and securely.
findings.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection by passing user-controlled data as a parameter to the execute method instead of concatenating it into the query string
findings.fixed_code: result = conn.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', (user_id,)).fetchall()

findings.title: RDS instance not encrypted
findings.description: The RDS instance is currently not encrypted, which poses a high security risk as sensitive data is stored in plaintext. Enabling encryption ensures that data at rest is protected. This can be achieved by setting the 'storage_encrypted' attribute to true in the aws_db_instance resource definition.
findings.fix_hint: Enable encryption for the RDS instance by setting the 'storage_encrypted' attribute to true

findings.title: S3 access logging disabled

To fix this, the logging configuration needs to be set on the S3 bucket resource. This can be done by adding a logging block to the resource definition, specifying the target bucket and prefix for the log files.
findings.fix_hint: Enable S3 access logging by setting the logging configuration on the S3 bucket resource

findings.title: S3 versioning disabled
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_21 check failed because S3 versioning was not enabled on the 'app_data' bucket, which can lead to data loss in case of accidental deletion or overwrite. Enabling versioning allows for the retrieval of previous versions of objects. This can be achieved by adding the 'versioning' block with 'enabled = true' to the 'aws_s3_bucket' resource.
findings.fix_hint: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket to track changes and prevent data loss

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: ec2:*
findings.description: The original policy had an implicit allow for all ec2 actions due to the lack of an explicit ec2 action, which is a security risk. The fixed code adds an explicit statement for the required ec2 actions, reducing the attack surface. This change ensures that only the necessary ec2 actions are allowed, rather than all of them.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the ec2:* action with specific ec2 actions that are required for the policy

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: s3:*
findings.description: The original policy grants full S3 access to all buckets, which is a security risk. To fix this, the S3 actions should be restricted to specific buckets or resources. The corrected policy snippet replaces the wildcard resource with a specific bucket ARN, reducing the attack surface.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict S3 access to specific buckets or resources instead of using a wildcard

findings.title: Ckv Aws 161
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_161 check failed because the AWS DB instance 'app_db' does not have deletion protection enabled, which can lead to accidental deletion of the database. Enabling deletion protection prevents the database from being deleted, even if the Terraform configuration is modified to delete it. This can be achieved by adding the 'deletion_protection' argument to the 'aws_db_instance' resource and setting it to 'true'
findings.fix_hint: Enable deletion protection for the AWS DB instance to prevent accidental deletion

attack_chains.title: Unrestricted SSH and Public RDS
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains initial access to the system via an unrestricted SSH connection, then accesses a publicly accessible RDS instance to extract sensitive data. This allows the attacker to gain full control over the database and potentially move laterally within the network.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains initial access to the system via an unrestricted SSH connection using finding c016064c in file xentinel-test-v2/infra/main.tf
Step 2: this gives them access to the publicly accessible RDS instance using finding bc331c3e in file xentinel-test-v2/infra/main.tf
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to only trusted IP addresses by updating the security group configuration in xentinel-test-v2/infra/main.tf

attack_chains.title: Tainted SQL String and Path Traversal
attack_chains.description: An attacker injects malicious SQL code into the application, then uses a path traversal vulnerability to access sensitive files and potentially gain control over the system. This allows the attacker to extract sensitive data and move laterally within the network.
steps: Step 1: attacker injects malicious SQL code into the application using finding 1ece43bd in file src/app.py
Step 2: this gives them access to sensitive files using finding d03bc491 in file src/app.py
attack_chains.remediation: Validate and sanitize user input to prevent SQL injection attacks by updating the code in src/app.py

attack_chains.title: Dangerous IAM Actions and Public S3 Bucket
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a dangerous IAM action to gain elevated privileges, then accesses a public S3 bucket to extract sensitive data. This allows the attacker to gain full control over the S3 bucket and potentially move laterally within the network.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains elevated privileges using finding 15e4731b in file iam/policy.json
Step 2: this gives them access to the public S3 bucket using finding f6a502b1 in file xentinel-test-v2/infra/main.tf
attack_chains.remediation: Remove the dangerous IAM action from the policy in iam/policy.json to prevent privilege escalation
